channel.title: Violations Watch: Yemen
channel.description: New incidents reported in Yemen. Most entries are unverified leads, not findings.

item.title: Houthis place the Sanaa home of Sheikh Naji Al-Qurtahi, a Yemeni-American, under seizure over his opposition to the group and his media activity, a lawyer says (Yemen Monitor)
item.description: Unverified lead (Medium priority). Sanaa, Yemen. Types: Persecution & repression, Destruction of property. Alleged perpetrator: Houthi (Ansar Allah) authorities. Disputed or caveats: Outlet close to the Yemeni government (a party to the war); based on a lawyer's account. 1 source. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-2024

item.title: Houthi-run health ministry says Saudi-led coalition attacks on Sanaa, Hodeidah, Hajjah, Taiz and Saada killed 41 civilians and injured 35, including women and children, over 48 hours (22–24 Nov)
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Yemen. Types: Killing of civilians, Air / drone / artillery strike. Alleged perpetrator: Saudi-led coalition. Reported casualties: 41 killed, 35 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Figures from Houthi officials, not independently verified. Democracy Now reports the Houthi claim as 41 civilians killed in a single day, including in Hodeidah and Lahij, with no injured figure and no mention of women or children; the 48-hour period, 35 injured, other governorates and women and children come from Saba and Press TV only. 9 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-2032

item.title: Buses and trucks hit in Wadi Mabaq, Lahj, on 23 Nov: Houthi-run Saba reports 25 dead or missing and six wounded and blames Saudi-led coalition strikes; Yemen's government blames Houthi shelling (AFP, Middle East Eye, Arab News)
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Wadi Mabaq (Hayjat al-Abd), Al-Maqatirah, Lahj, Yemen. Types: Killing of civilians, Air / drone / artillery strike. Alleged perpetrator: Disputed: Saudi-led coalition (per Houthi authorities) or Houthis (per Yemeni government). Reported casualties: 10-26 killed, 6+ injured. Disputed or caveats: Tolls from parties to the conflict and unnamed local officials, not independently verified: Houthi-run Saba reports 25 dead or missing; AFP, citing local officials, reports 26 killed, of whom one official said 12 were Houthi fighters and 14 civilians. Houthis blame Saudi-led coalition aircraft; government forces blame Houthi attack. 7 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-1872

item.title: Houthi shelling and sniper fire in Taiz on 22 Nov kill two civilians and injure up to eight, including a girl (Yemeni army, SANA)
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Kahlan, Al-Aqrud, Taiz, Yemen. Types: Killing of civilians, Air / drone / artillery strike. Alleged perpetrator: Houthis (Ansar Allah). Reported casualties: 2 killed, 6-8 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Figures from Yemeni government forces (a party to the conflict). Arab News dates the Houthi missile strike on a house in Kahlan to 23 Nov and reports two killed and seven wounded, plus a woman shot by a sniper; other reports give 22 Nov and 6 to 8 injured. Arab News does not mention a child among the victims. 3 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-1871

item.title: Houthi-run health ministry says a Saudi air strike on a boat carrying more than 25 displaced people from Ras al-Ara to Khays, near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, killed 19 and wounded four, mostly women and children; not independently verified
item.description: Unverified lead (Critical priority). Ras al-Ara coast (Bab al-Mandeb), Lahj, Yemen. Types: Killing of civilians, Air / drone / artillery strike. Alleged perpetrator: Saudi-led coalition (as reported by Houthi-run authorities). Reported casualties: 19 killed, 4 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Figures and attribution only from the Houthi-run health ministry (spokesperson Anis al-Asbahi), Al Masirah and SABA (party-affiliated); Al Masirah says 8 children and 6 women among the dead; reported by Sigmalive and New Straits Times as allegations not independently verified; no Saudi or coalition response found. 7 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-1372
